title: Bahai Badi Calendar
intro: The Badi calendar is the religious calendar of the Bahá'í Faith.
summary: A solar calendar organised around nineteen months and an intercalary interval.
epoch: The Bahá'í Era (B.E.) begins in 1844, linked to the declaration of the Báb. Naw-Rúz is the New Year.
epoch_heading: THE BAHÁ'Í ERA AND NEW YEAR
year_rule: Nineteen months each contain nineteen days (361 days). Ayyam-i-Ha adds four or five days between months 18 and 19, bringing the year to 365 or 366 days.
after_note: After day 19 of Mulk comes the intercalary interval, followed by Ala 1. Month names use simple Roman-letter spellings; transliterations vary.
history: The Báb introduced the Badi calendar and Bahá'u'lláh confirmed it. Its month names reflect attributes of God. Religious days begin at sunset.
limits: Years 1–171 B.E. use a fixed 21 March start. From year 172 the provider models Tehran equinox/sunset within Gregorian years 1000–3000, with fixed-rule continuation outside. It does not certify all historic observances or distant predictions.
